# the contributor audit: shared-source cap signatures and adaptive credit

Source: `candidate c7b6ab042f325988`.
Result: PASS. The independent exact verifier was rerun:1,746 checks PASS.

The conditional gluing keeps the two original relation laws, hence every
actual uniform source marginal and both barycentric target identities.
The pointwise hitting costs in the four target-event states are exactly
0,c1,c2,c12. In the double state the shared source or one exclusive source
from each relation suffices; the minimal costs are a and b+c. Thus the
expected shared-source cost is counted once and yields the stated bound.
The incidence-sharpness claim is correctly restricted to Boolean data,
not arbitrary convex realizations.

The fixed packing LP is solved by prioritizing the larger event marginal.
Its second coefficient is c12-c1 (or reversed), so subtracting it from
the adaptive bound gives rho times the smaller directed crossing mass.
The conditional Frechet bound yields exactly the two positive-part
expectations in (8); conditional independence gives (9). Both use one
actual coupling for all caps.

The8-by8 conditional transportation polytope has a finite list of basic
feasible candidates after removing a redundant equality. Their entries
are linear in the Borel marginals, including degenerate zero entries.
Selecting the first feasible cost-minimizer is Borel. Further conditioning
the original relation kernels on their signatures and then gluing them
realizes the SINGLE optimized weighted objective while keeping both
original laws. No incompatible separate cap optimizers enter.

The rectangle widths2,-1,-1 give the actual concave section roof. The
two target widths3/2 and1 have directed crossing area1/6 in a square of
area4, hence probability1/24, intersection11/24, and credit13/6 rather
than2 on each of two specified caps. The verifier supplies the same joint
three-bit table for all three caps. Actual source captured mass may be
larger; no global depth or genuine criticality of this menu is claimed.
The residual-root inequalities and coincident-copy/parity-forest scope
checks are valid. The three-base(1/4,1,1) example has no second relation,
so the new theorem correctly makes no claim to repair it.

Minor reference correction requested: cite the newly proved multi-input
coupling source for that optional density-ceiling input; the present
hitting-cost theorem itself works with any two given actual couplings.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
